answer: Based on the node2vec paper (Grover & Leskovec, 2016), DFS-like sampling does not reduce variance in characterizing 1-hop nodes relative to the source. That property belongs to BFS-like sampling (small return parameter p and large in-out parameter q), because BFS walks keep sampling the same immediate neighbourhood and so give low-variance estimates of 1-hop nodes. DFS-like sampling (large p, small q) explores farther, outward parts of the network. It captures macro-level homophily and community structure, but it has higher variance for the immediate neighbourhood. The question's premise therefore appears mistaken, and no condition makes DFS reduce 1-hop variance.
